author: Patrick Butler and Will Parman
description:
Experts say trend across England probably reflects swifter access to diagnoses as wealthier families go private

Some of the most affluent areas of England have had the sharpest rises in the proportion of young people claiming disability benefits for ADHD and autism since the pandemic, according to new research.

Claims for the personal independence payment (Pip) benefit for these health conditions were typically proportionally far higher in deprived areas with higher rates of poverty, low educational outcomes and insecure employment.

Continue reading...
title: Young people’s Pip claims for ADHD and autism ‘rising fastest in affluent areas’

author: Andrew Gregory Health editor
description:
Changes could save £33bn and result in average of four extra years of good health for people, report says

The NHS in England could prevent 20,000 deaths and save £33bn a year by cutting red tape and boosting productivity, a report says.

Research by the Health Foundation found the health service has been held back for decades by excessive regulation, short-term planning and insufficient capability to deliver major change.

Continue reading...
title: Cut NHS red tape and boost productivity to prevent 20,000 early deaths a year in England, report urges

author: Associated Press
description:
Supreme court, which has twice blocked maps from being used in November, likely to have final say in legal fight

A long-running legal fight over Missouri’s congressional map took another turn Monday when a federal appeals panel ruled in favor of new districts backed by Donald Trump, even though the US supreme court has blocked those districts from being used in the November election.

A three-judge panel of the 8th US circuit court of appeals said Missouri should use the new Republican-drawn US House districts in the November election, just as the state did in its August primary. To revert to its prior districts for the general election would violate the US constitution, the appeals judges said.

Continue reading...
title: Appeals court rules in favor of Trump-backed Missouri congressional maps

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Tanya Plibersek says we need to use ‘all of our big systems’ to better tackle domestic violence

Tanya Plibersek, the minister for social services, said she was struck that a spate of alleged domestic violence incidents this weekend weren’t previously identified by police.

All of these big points of contact as potential systems where we can identify that there is a risk that there’s family, domestic or sexual violence happening and be able to intervene earlier.

It’s not just about funding. There’s also, I think, a much broader role for our community. …

Support for victims and survivors, making sure that we’re
title: Australia news live: Albanese signs declaration with world leaders urging human control over AI; city of Sydney bans smartglasses

author: Pippa Crerar in New York
description:
Andy Burnham says he will urge Donald Trump to bring an end to conflict with Iran

The UK has agreed to provide defensive air support to Saudi Arabia to help counter Houthi fighters and restore stability in the Middle East while driving down the cost of living at home, Andy Burnham has said, ahead of his first meeting with Donald Trump.

The prime minister said he had agreed to a request for air-to-air refuelling of Saudi jets to defend energy infrastructure against the Iran-backed rebels and help keep oil flowing from the Gulf to ease global economic turmoil.

Continue reading...
title: UK to give support to Saudi jets in attempt to counter Houthi fighters

author: Alexandra Topping and Peter Walker
description:
At Lib Dems’ conference in Brighton, leader will accuse Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and ‘tech bros’ to solve problem

Ed Davey is to call for a global nuclear-style non-proliferation treaty to halt the development of super-intelligent AI when he makes his keynote speech at the Liberal Democrat conference, accusing Andy Burnham of relying on Donald Trump and “tech bros” to solve the problem.

When he addresses the faithful on the final day of the gathering in Brighton, the party leader will call for a global pause on super-intelligent AI, comparing it to a nuclear arms race that could result in technology that could “destroy us all”.

Continue reading...
title: Halt super-intelligent AI with non-proliferation treaty, Ed Davey to say

author: Jess Cartner-Morley
description:
Textile designer brings florals, vines and smiley doodles to brand’s luxury checks for one-off paired collection

Burberry and Celia Birtwell are both national treasures of sorts. One is Britain’s grandest luxury name, the other the textile designer who dressed bohemian 1960s London in her prints and has a place in art history as David Hockney’s favourite muse.

The Burberry designer Daniel Lee has always loved Birtwell’s prints. When the two met this spring, he fell for “her energy, and her zest for life”, and a one-off Burberry-meets-Birtwell collection that closed London fashion week was born.

Continue reading...
title: Celia Birtwell ‘humanises’ Burberry in London fashion week closing show

author: Sara Sneath in New York and Oliver Milman
description:
Prime ministers of Australia and Iceland discuss effects on their countries even as some shy away in face of war and inflation

World political leaders are descending on New York for the UN general assembly and some of them are putting the climate crisis on the agenda as they spoke on Monday at the start of the city’s annual Climate Week.

This year’s Climate Week – which runs alongside UNGA – comes after months of extreme heat in large parts of the world including Europe and the US, wildfires in Africa, flash flooding in Asia and a record-breaking El Niño.

Continue reading...
title: World leaders address climate crisis before UN meet amid record-breaking El-Niño

author: Lucy Campbell and agency
description:
James Eaton, 51, faces life in prison after jury rejects insanity defense rooted in claims he was acting on orders from US and Israeli intelligence

A jury has convicted a Vermont man of attempted murder in the shootings of three Palestinian college students who were walking near his home, rejecting an insanity defense rooted in his claims that he was acting on orders from the CIA and Mossad.

Jason Eaton, 51, faces up to life in prison over the November 2023 attack near the University of Vermont campus in Burlington, which left Hisham Awartani paralyzed from the waist down and wounded his friends, Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid.

Continue reading...
title: Vermont man convicted of attempted murder of three Palestinian students

author: Coral Murphy Marcos
description:
California man charged with misdemeanor battery in Burbank over incident sending three patrons to hospital

A 34-year-old man from California has been arrested after allegedly pepper-spraying a person at a movie theater who was using his cellphone during the film, according to authorities.

Police arrested Matthew Ware on 15 September after purportedly pepper spraying a patron at the AMC Burbank 16 who was using his cellphone, while two other moviegoers nearby also experienced irritation from the pepper spray, according to the Burbank police department. All three people were treated at a local hospital.

Continue reading...
title: Moviegoer using phone during film pepper-sprayed in LA, police say

author: Ariana Baio in New York
description:
ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC decline to participate after presidential ban that prompted wide condemnation

Major US TV news networks agreed to refuse to air coverage of Donald Trump’s White House after the administration banned certain media outlets including CNN from the grounds.

The ban left CNN unable to fulfill its duties as Monday’s White House designated pool broadcaster.

Continue reading...
title: US TV networks suspend White House pool coverage over Trump media ban

author: Associated Press
description:
Immigration agency’s move makes it harder for lawyers and family to find detainees, in line with stringent Trump policy

US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has stopped publicly revealing where it is holding thousands of detainees who are subject to final deportation orders, an unannounced move that has made it far more difficult for lawyers and relatives to find them, according to current and former officials familiar with the practice.

ICE removed those detainees from its online detainee locator system on 15 September, according to three current and former ICE officials who spoke to the Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to discuss the change. Several lawyers contacted by the AP confirmed their clients vanished
title: ICE hides locations of thousands of detainees with final removal orders

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Super El-Niño has already broken temperature records and is predicted to bring an extremely wet winter to the state

  • ‘Jaw-dropping’ El Niño bursts through temperature record months before peak

California is bracing for a record breaking El Niño that is expected to bring severe winter storms and flooding across the state, with the state’s governor declaring a state of emergency in anticipation of extreme weather in the months ahead.

The global climate phenomenon known as a “super El Niño” is already breaking temperature records and drawing predictions of an extre
title: California braces for record El Niño storms as governor declares emergency

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
New rules also include a ban near schools and childcare centres and require them to source their own renewable energy

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Datacentres in Victoria will be banned in residential areas and required to use renewable energy and contribute to the community, under new state government rules.

On Tuesday, the premier, Ben Carroll, will release the government’s sustainable datacentre action plan, after it was approved by cabinet on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Datacentres in Victoria to be banned in residential areas

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Senator Ron Wyden calls for swift action after GAO report finds systems guiding US aircraft vulnerable to interference

A congressional watchdog has warned the systems guiding US aircraft are open to interference and deception as flights into three busy airports in the country’s north east US were halted by a radio equipment problem.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a ground stop at about 10am on Monday for Newark Liberty international, Philadelphia international and Teterboro airports, saying some radio frequencies at the Philadelphia terminal radar approach control (Tracon) were affected until the early afternoon. Arrivals and departures at Newark were delayed, and the agency has not said what caused the outage.

Continue reading...
title: Flights halted at three US airports as watchdog warns over hacking threat

author: Alice Speri
description:
Students faced prison terms and thousands of dollars in restitution over campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza

Five Stanford University students who faced prison sentences and thousands of dollars in restitution in connection to a campus protest against Israel’s war on Gaza had all charges dropped on Monday.

The students also had their restitution severely reduced, ending a two-year legal saga that also saw the lead prosecutor in the case removed by the court.

Continue reading...
title: Charges dropped against Stanford students over pro-Palestine protest

author: Associated Press in Bogotá
description:
Wildfire forces evacuations and burns through mountains surrounding Villa de Leyva in the north-east

Colombian authorities declared a public calamity as a wildfire burned through mountains surrounding one of the country’s best-known colonial towns in the north-east, scorching large swaths of vegetation and forcing evacuations.

Nearly 20 active fires are burning across the South American country. Dry conditions have increased fire danger in Colombia as it braces for the effects of El Niño, which can help wildfires spread.

Continue reading...
title: Colombia declares public calamity as wildfire threatens popular tourist area

author: Richard Luscombe and Lucy Campbell
description:
Republican congresswoman rejects ethics complaint and says allegations part of ‘politically motivated’ hit campaign

Lauren Boebert, the firebrand Republican subject of a House ethics complaint that she had sex with three staff members, and paid one to keep quiet, has said the allegations are untrue – and part of a “politically motivated” campaign against her.

Boebert’s denials came through a formal statement from her office, which said “the congresswoman rejects the claims as utterly false”. She also published a verbose video rant on social media in which she accused the person who filed the document as a “sloppy, desperate, obsessive hack
title: Lauren Boebert says claims of sexual relationships with staffers ‘utterly false’

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Iowa senator Chuck Grassley calls for embargo on diesel exports as tariffs and Iran war drive up costs for sector

Donald Trump is facing growing calls, including from within his own party, to boost support for US farmers as his administration faces mounting anger over its treatment of the agricultural sector.

Republican senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa called on the US president to place an embargo on diesel exports this weekend and help farmers grapple with high prices.

Continue reading...
title: Key ally urges Trump to back US farmers amid anger over rising prices

author: Maya Yang
description:
Gilbert’s family says he died ‘peacefully in his sleep’ months after My Friends Over You musician shared stage four cancer diagnosis

Guitarist Chad Gilbert – a founding member of the US rock band New Found Glory that doled out the early 2000s anthem My Friends Over You – has died aged 45.

Gilbert’s family announced his death on Sunday, saying that he “passed away peacefully in his sleep” and “left this world surrounded by friends and family and took his final breaths with his wife and mother by his side, just as he wished”.

Continue reading...
title: Chad Gilbert, New Found Glory’s founding guitarist, dies aged 45

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Ahead of United Nations meeting, prime minister says Australians knows the impact of global heating as well as anyone

Australia understands the dangers of global warming and the urgency of climate action as much as any other country, Anthony Albanese has said in a keynote speech ahead of the United Nations general assembly.

Speaking at the opening of the Climate Week event at the United Nations in New York on Monday, the prime minister said Australians had experienced the impact of climate change up close with a series of disastrous bushfires and floods in the past decades.

Continue reading...
title: No avoiding the cost of inaction on climate, Anthony Albanese says in New York

author: Bob Burton
description:
Salmon companies operating in Tasmanian marine areas deployed almost 1,800 explosives in first half of 2026, government figures reveal

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More than 150,000 underwater explosives have been used to deter seals at Tasmanian salmon farms since 2016, according to new government data.

Department of Natural Resources and Environment (NRE Tas) data released last week revealed salmon companies directed almost 1,800 underwater explosives at seals at fish farms in the first half of 2026.
title: More than 150,000 underwater explosives used to deter seals at Tasmanian salmon farms since 2016

author: Donna Lu Assistant editor, climate, environment and science
description:
New study describes two species, Anchiale robusta and Anchiale mabiensis, both found in far north Queensland

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two new large stick insect species have been identified by Australian researchers, in a discovery they say illustrates how little we still understand about insect diversity.

The two species, both found in far north Queensland, are described in a study published in Austral Entomology.

Continue reading...
title: Discovery of new Australian stick insect species reveals case of mistaken identity

author: Associated Press
description:
Officials say man was critically injured and officer was wounded in Yom Kippur incident near Belleville synagogue

A police officer and a man were wounded in an exchange of gunfire on Sunday near a synagogue in Ontario as members of the Jewish community marked Yom Kippur, authorities said. The man was hospitalized in life-threatening condition.

The Canadian province’s special investigations unit said the exchange of gunfire happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue in Belleville, Ontario, about 110 miles (160km) east of Toronto. Belleville police said the officer encountered the man at about 7.10pm and that both were taken to a hospital.

Continue reading...
title: Man and police officer wounded in exchange of gunfire near Ontario synagogue

author: Guardian staff
description:
Doula stopped to assist couple with birth while first responders were also stuck in traffic and arrived on foot

A woman stuck in heavy traffic in San Francisco went into labor and gave birth to a healthy baby girl, local authorities have said.

The San Francisco fire department said in a statement that a couple had been snarled in heavy congestion near the city’s Golden Gate Park when they were forced to pull over due to the imminent birth.

Continue reading...
title: ‘So surreal’: woman gives birth while stuck in heavy San Francisco traffic

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Walter Moorhead, 74, jailed on suspicion of manslaughter after allegedly shooting a woman while hunting in Delaware

A Maryland hunter was recently jailed on suspicion of manslaughter after he allegedly fatally shot a woman whom he mistook for a deer, according to authorities in Delaware.

Walter Moorhead, 74, was hunting from a ground blind in a field near Ellendale, Delaware, at about 7.40pm on Friday when he believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, state police said in a statement. Yet it was actually a woman whom Moorhead fired at and struck as she walked across the field with two children, the statement added.
title: US hunter charged after fatally shooting woman he mistook for a deer, police say

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Police responded to altercation and found injured man and another person who identified himself as a federal agent

Authorities in Illinois are investigating a case on Sunday in which a US citizen was detained by federal immigration agents before ending up at a hospital with injuries.

It came the same day that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) shot and seriously wounded a man in Austin, Texas.

Continue reading...
title: Illinois authorities investigate possible ICE wounding of US citizen

author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
description:
Friedrich Merz clinging to power after Christian Democratic Union loses two state elections

  • Europe live – latest updates

Germany’s beleaguered leader, Friedrich Merz, has sought to shore up support for his flagging chancellorship among senior members of his conservative party after its drubbing at the polls in two state elections.

Merz, who has vowed his fractious coalition government will plough ahead with an unpopular reform agenda, held an early meeting in Berlin with the Christian Democratic Union (CDU)’s leadership on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: German chancellor meets CDU leaders to shore up support after more defeats

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Blow to John Healey before budget as UK households face ‘notable strain’ on their finances

  • Business live – latest updates

Fears of a steep rise in mortgage payments and increasing job insecurity have sent UK consumer confidence tumbling to a three-month low, according to a leading survey.

In a blow to John Healey before next month’s budget, the S&P Global consumer sentiment index dropped to 42.7 in September from 42.9 in August, indicating “a notable strain on financial confidence across UK households”.

Continue reading...
title: Fears over interest rate rise and jobs send UK consumer confidence to three-year low

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Three news outlets to sue in case that could come this week after Trump said he would ban them from White House grounds

  • Sign up for US Breaking News emails

A US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer shot and wounded a Venezuelan man on Sunday afternoon in Texas’s capital city, Austin, prompting demonstrations at the scene against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign.

The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as
title: CNN, MS Now and Politico to sue over White House ban – US politics live

author: Steven Morris
description:
Eco-moorings help to restore seagrass in just five years, boosting sealife such as seahorses, eels and crabs

One of the UK’s most precious underwater habitats – Dorset’s seagrass meadows – is recovering thanks to “eco moorings” designed to prevent the seabed being ripped up, a study has revealed.

Scars caused by traditional anchors in some areas of seagrass in Studland Bay have almost entirely vanished, which is boosting the number of seahorses that thrive in the submerged meadows.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Inredibly enouraging’: healing the scars of traditional anchors in Dorset’s seagrass meadows

author: Michael Sainato
description:
Several workers say they’re opting to go without health coverage due to premium costs soaring this year

Starbucks workers say their health insurance premiums have soared this year, in some cases more than doubling, according to a recent survey conducted by Starbucks Workers United.

The survey of more than 130 Starbucks workers in both unionized and non-unionized stores, shared exclusively with the Guardian, found baristas are experiencing significant hikes in costs for their health insurance coverage starting 1 October.

Continue reading...
title: Starbucks baristas reel from surges in health insurance costs: ‘I’m considering a second job’

author: Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Watchdog says users may have been unaware their information was used to target adverts or infer their interests

Google has been fined more than €400m (£345m) over the way it processed users’ location data, following claims that the tech giant had manipulated users into agreeing to be constantly tracked on their mobile phones.

The fine, by Ireland’s Data Protection Commission (DPC), comes after complaints from multiple European consumer organisations that Google was following every step users took.

Continue reading...
title: Google is fined more than €400m by Irish regulator over its use of location data

author: Jem Bartholomew
description:
Thousands of people deported from the US to countries where they have no connections. Plus, European spy chiefs warn of Moscow action against Nato

  • Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning.

After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands of people deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries.

At what scale are third-country deportations happening? Since returning to office in 2025, Donald Trump’s administration has deported more than
title: Banished to alien lands – Trump’s secret deportation deals | First Thing

author: Deborah Cole in Berlin
description:
Chancellor acknowledges disastrous state election results but vow to push on is likely to further alienate voters, and his own party

• Europe live – latest updates

Friedrich Merz called it a “disaster”, and that was even before the full scale of the catastrophe for himself and his conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) came into view after Sunday’s state elections.

In what one outlet called a “power move”, the German chancellor made a highly unusual televised speech just minutes after polls closed in the states of Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, attempting to get a
title: Latest German election humiliation puts Merz on borrowed time as CDU unrest grows

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
British Airways and easyJet among those to cancel or delay services after air traffic control fault at Prestwick

  • Business live – latest updates

Flights are being disrupted in parts of the UK after National Air Traffic Services was hit by its second technical issue in a fortnight.

A number of departing and arriving flights at Scottish airports have been severely delayed, with disruption affecting Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England.

Continue reading...
title: Flights cancelled at airports in Scotland, northern England and Northern Ireland

author: Patrick Commins
description:
The population is ageing and we’re having fewer babies. Labor should keep that in mind as the migration debate rages

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The intergenerational report lays bare how today’s growing anti-migration rhetoric clashes with a future where we need to attract people from overseas to help grow the economy and pay for our ageing population.

The “replacement” fertility rate is 2.1 children per woman – this is the average number of births to keep the population steady without migration and we’ve been below this level for 50 years.
title: Think Australia would be better off with less migration? The numbers tell a different story

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
Hollywood actress appears in NSW supreme court in Sydney for the latest lawsuit over her directorial debut

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Hollywood star Rebel Wilson had a “last chance” phone call with her film’s co-producers over a dispute about up-front costs and her $1m fee, a judge has heard.

The Pitch Perfect and Bridesmaids star appeared in the New South Wales supreme court in Sydney on Monday in the latest lawsuit over her directorial debut, a musical comedy named The Deb.

Continue reading...
title: Rebel Wilson back in court as The Deb producers sue star over allegedly blocking film

author: Achol Arok
description:
Five other people in house at the time of the shooting were unharmed, police say

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

An 11-year-old boy has been taken to hospital in a serious condition after being shot in a home in Sydney’s north-west.

Emergency services responded to reports of a shooting at a property in Norwest at about 5pm on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Boy, 11, in serious condition after being shot in face and neck in Sydney home

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Intergenerational report predicts that in four decades’ time, more Australians will be dying than being born each year

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor says better investment in early childhood education and care, such as a possible move to universal access for families, is a better way to address Australia’s declining birthrate, rejecting the need for a new “baby bonus”.

Monday’s intergenerational report showed that more Australians will be dying than being born in 40 years’ time, a point already reached by countries including South Korea, Italy, Germany and Japa
title: Universal early childhood education better than baby bonus to increase Australia’s birthrate, Labor says

author: Ben Doherty and AAP
description:
Court also hears from four people who say they didn’t witness alleged offence against another complainant

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One of Alan Jones’s accusers has had his allegation withdrawn by prosecutors, with one charge of indecent assault against a 17-year-old boy dramatically dropped from the former broadcaster’s trial.

The allegation, brought by a complainant pseudonymised as F, was withdrawn by the prosecution in a Sydney court on Monday afternoon.
title: Teen complainant withdrawn from Alan Jones trial bringing number of alleged victims to five

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Texts reveal Sharangan Maheswaran had ‘an explanation ready’ but was worried about picture taken with premier prompted by ‘dumb’ Christian Ellis

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A Labor councillor feared his presence at a Liberal fundraiser attended by Dominic Perrottet would result in him being forced to give evidence to the New South Wales anti-corruption commission, the watchdog has heard.
title: ‘Oh shit’: Labor councillor who attended 2021 Liberal fundraiser was worried about potential Icac inquiry, Icac hears

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
Temperatures in Sydney’s outer west peaked at 35C and 32C in the city on Monday before a cool change from the south-east

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Sydney and parts of New South Wales have sweltered through an “unseasonably warm” weekend, with temperatures climbing more than 10C above the September average, before a cool change swept much of the coast on Monday.

The early burst of heat, part of a classic “
title: Sydney and parts of NSW swelter through temperatures in the 30s before plummeting 10C within hours

author: Alice Speri
description:
Media workers are grappling with increasingly volatile press climate in US, with some detained and even deported

  • Banished: Trump’s secret deportation deals

  • What is Trump’s third-country deportation policy?

As hundreds of masked and armed US federal agents besieged the streets of Minneapolis, turning the midwestern city into the frontline of the Trump administration’s unprecedented crackdown on immigration, the independent photographer John Abernathy was documenting one of the protests that had become a daily occurrence when Immigration and Customs Enforcement tackled him.

A photograph of him on
title: Freedom oppressed: the journalists caught up in Trump’s ICE crackdown

author: Kat Wong
description:
The 31-year-old former police officer has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder as his trial begins in Sydney’s supreme court

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A former police officer allegedly developed an “infatuation and obsession” with one of his victims, and disguised himself as an Uber Eats rider before shooting two men, a court has heard.

Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter as his trial began in Sydn
title: NSW cop Beau Lamarre-Condon allegedly disguised himself as Uber Eats rider before double murder, court hears

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Seventh intergenerational report also outlines how Australia is at cusp of an uncertain age of artificial intelligence

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

There will be more Australians dying than being born in 40 years’ time, according to the government’s latest intergenerational report, which lays bare the fundamental challenges of managing an ageing population at a time of rapid change and lower economic growth.

The country’s seventh IGR also outlines how Australia is at the cusp of a n
title: More Australians will be dying than being born in 40 years as major report predicts future of lower growth
